title: Discrete-Time Heat-Flux Rigidity Under C2 Boundary Regularity
content: Let Ω ⊂ RN, N ≥ 2, be a bounded connected domain, and let u(t) = et∆D 1 be the Dirichlet heat evolution of the constant initial temperature. We prove that if the exterior normal derivative ∂νu(·,tj) is constant on ∂Ω along a sequence tj ↓ 0, then Ω is a ball, assuming only ∂Ω ∈ C2. This answers, in the classical curvature regime, the finite-regularity question posed by Cavallina and Pinamonti for their short-time discrete-flux theorem. The key result is the uniform expansion ∂νu(y,t) = −1(πt)-½ + H(y)/2 + o(1) as t ↓ 0, where H is the sum of the principal curvatures with respect to the inward unit normal. More quantitatively, the remainder is bounded by C(√t + ωH(C√t)) , with ωH the modulus of continuity of H. If ∂Ω ∈ C2,α, this gives the rate O(tα/2). The proof uses a boundary-layer parametrix, ambient Euclidean mollification of a normal extension of H, and an L∞-to-C1 estimate for the Dirichlet heat semigroup. The ambient regularization avoids differentiating the metrics of parallel hypersurfaces and therefore does not require third derivatives of the boundary-layer parametrix, ambient Euclidean mollification of a normal extension of H, and an L∞-to-C1 estimate for the Dirichlet heat semigroup.
